hints: Count the bases in CGGGCCCCGCGG. There are 12 bases, so split them into four groups of three to see the four DNA triplets that will be transcribed.
This is the strand that is transcribed (the template), so the mRNA will be complementary to it, not identical. Remember C pairs with G, G pairs with C, and A pairs with U in RNA.
walkthrough:
**Split the DNA into triplets**

You have 12 bases, which makes 4 codons. Reading left to right, split them into threes.

$$CGG \; GCC \; CCG \; CGG$$

**Transcribe DNA template to mRNA**

The strand shown is transcribed, so it is the template strand. Build the complementary mRNA using C-G, G-C, and remember RNA has no T.

$$DNA: CGG \; GCC \; CCG \; CGG$$
$$mRNA: GCC \; CGG \; GGC \; GCC$$

**Translate mRNA to amino acids**

Now use the table to read each mRNA codon. GCC = Ala, CGG = Arg, GGC = Gly, GCC = Ala.

So the order is Ala-Arg-Gly-Ala, which is option B.

options.A: Incorrect. This mixes up transcription and misses the correct complementary pairing, giving Cys from UGC which is not produced here.
options.B: Correct. Complementary mRNA is GCC-CGG-GGC-GCC, which translates to Ala-Arg-Gly-Ala using the table.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the common trap of reading the DNA directly as if it were mRNA (CGG = Arg, GCC = Ala, etc). You must first make the complementary mRNA.
options.D: Incorrect. This also fails to form the correct complementary mRNA and incorrectly includes Thr (ACG), which does not appear.
